plant.compliance: Protected variety (labelled cov); PBR number not confirmed.
plant.cvs: 'Aurea' – golden-yellow leaves · f. angustifolia – narrow, willow-like leaves
plant.foliage: evergreen; aromatic, glossy dark green lance-shaped leaves
plant.hardinessNote: Hardy through an average UK winter, approximately -10 to -5°C; pot-grown plants need shelter in hard frosts.
plant.pollination: not applicable; grown for foliage, the species bears male and female flowers on separate plants
plant.prune: Trim to shape in summer. Cut out frost-browned shoots in late spring once new growth shows.
plant.resilience: Copes well with clipping and pot culture; leaves scorch in cold winds and hard frost. Pests: bay sucker, scale insects, leaf spot.

plant.toxicity: Leaves are a culinary herb for people, but bay is listed as toxic to dogs, cats and horses if eaten, causing vomiting and diarrhoea. Not the same plant as cherry laurel.
uncertain: height and spread: blank. LITTLE RAGU is sold as a compact or dwarf bay, but I cannot state its mature dimensions with confidence. Check the breeder or label.
hardiness: H4 is the RHS rating for the species Laurus nobilis, applied here to the cultivar. Confirm there is no separate cultivar rating.

compliance: 'cov' indicates a protected or patented variety; the UK PBR number and holder (thought to be Monrovia) are not confirmed. Also check whether Laurus nobilis appears on the current Xylella host list for plant passport purposes.
growthSpeed: 6 is judged from the compact cultivar habit plus the slow-to-steady species rate; not confirmed for this cultivar.
clay: blank. The species prefers well-drained soil and dislikes winter wet, but tolerance of heavy clay is not established for this cultivar.
sunMin: 50 is judged from the species tolerating part shade.
pestRisk: 10 is judged from bay sucker and scale being common on UK bays.
toxicity: pet toxicity rests on the ASPCA listing for bay laurel as remembered; severity in small amounts is likely mild.
cvs: lists sibling forms of the species only; other compact bay selections were not confirmed.
peak: Jan-Dec reflects year-round foliage interest. The flowers are minor and appear in spring.
plant.uses: Patio containers · herb gardens · small gardens · culinary leaves · formal clipped shapes
plant.visual: Compact, dense, aromatic evergreen bay · glossy dark green culinary leaves all year · small yellowish spring flowers
plant.water: Water pots regularly in summer and keep them barely moist in winter. Plants in the ground need little once established.
